directAnswer: That behavior is HDMI-CEC: the console sends a power-on command over HDMI. Turn off HDMI Device Link / HDMI-CEC on the PlayStation, Xbox, or Switch, or disable CEC / Auto power on on the TV (often branded Bravia Sync, Anynet+, SIMPLINK, VIERA Link, or EasyLink). A soundbar in the chain can forward the same command.
summary: CEC is useful for one-remote control and annoying when a console, Apple TV, or soundbar wakes the whole stack. Fix it on the device that is sending the power-on, not by unplugging HDMI every night.

sections.heading: What HDMI-CEC is doing
sections.body: Consumer Electronics Control is a one-wire protocol in the HDMI cable. Devices use it to power the TV on, switch inputs, and volume-control a soundbar. Names differ by brand: Sony Bravia Sync, Samsung Anynet+, LG SIMPLINK, Panasonic VIERA Link, Philips EasyLink, plus generic HDMI-CEC or HDMI Control. The TV, AVR/soundbar, and console each have their own switch — any one of them can still turn the TV on if it is left enabled.

sections.heading: Break the chain at the noisiest device
sections.body: If only the PlayStation wakes the TV, disable HDMI Device Link on the PS5. If everything wakes everything (AVR + TV + console), turn CEC off on the soundbar/AVR first, then the TV’s auto power on. You can leave CEC on for volume and still disable device auto power on on many TVs.

steps.title: Turn it off on the console
steps.detail: PS5: Settings → System → HDMI → turn off Enable HDMI Device Link. Xbox: Profile & system → Settings → General → TV & display options → Advanced → turn off HDMI-CEC (Device control). Nintendo Switch: System Settings → TV Settings → turn off Match TV Power State.

steps.title: Turn off CEC / auto power on the TV
steps.detail: Open the TV’s HDMI or External inputs menu and disable HDMI-CEC / Bravia Sync / Anynet+ / SIMPLINK. Also look for Auto power on, TV auto on, or Power on with HDMI. You can keep HDMI-CEC for the soundbar volume and still disable auto power on if the TV offers both.

steps.title: Check the soundbar or AVR
steps.detail: If HDMI goes Console → bar → TV (ARC/eARC), the bar often has HDMI-CEC / Control for HDMI. Disable device power linking there. One leftover CEC device is enough to turn the TV on.

steps.title: If it still happens, isolate the HDMI port
steps.detail: Unplug other CEC gadgets (streaming stick, soundbar) one at a time. Try another HDMI input — some TVs enable CEC per jack. A cheap HDMI splitter that does not handle CEC cleanly can also spam power commands; connect the console directly to test.

faqs.question: Can I keep using the TV remote for PlayStation volume?
faqs.answer: Volume usually needs CEC or ARC. You can often disable power-on linking and leave HDMI control / ARC on. If the TV only has one CEC switch, you choose between convenience and the TV staying off.

faqs.question: Why does the TV also switch to the game input?
faqs.answer: Same CEC feature (one-touch play). Disabling Device Link / CEC stops both the power-on and the input grab.

faqs.question: Does 4K/120Hz or VRR require CEC?
faqs.answer: No. Picture mode, HDMI 2.1 features, and ALLM are separate. Turning CEC off does not block 4K or 120Hz.

caveats: Some TVs re-enable Anynet+/SIMPLINK after a firmware update. Recheck once if the problem comes back.
Game Mode and HDMI-CEC are different menus — turning off Game Mode will not stop the TV waking.
